guideline: Unavailable dates.

When a day or several days a

fields.before: Calendars display the days of a selected month and highlight the current day. They support navigating to past or future months and selecting a specific date.
fields.after:
Unavailable dates.

When a day or several days are unavailable within the calendar popover, each day should display a strikethrough to help the user understand that they cannot select it. Disabled days use a distinct gray style to clearly differentiate them from unavailable days. When the calendar prevents selection of past dates, this visual treatment helps users distinguish disabled days from those marked as unavailable.

entries.name: guideline: Why unavailable and disabled days are necessary.

fields.before: An array of days that are displayed in the current calendar view. This includes:
fields.after:
Why unavailable and disabled days are necessary.

In a date selection system, users often need to distinguish between dates that cannot be selected and dates that are simply inactive. Supporting both states improves clarity and prevents errors. Here's an example scenario: A potential guest is browsing a calendar to book a stay at a vacation rental. Unavailable dates: Days when the rental is already booked or blocked by the owner. These appear with a strikethrough, indicating they cannot be selected. Disabled dates: Past dates that are no longer valid for booking. These appear visually distinct (gray style) to show they are inactive. Guests see unavailable dates marked clearly so they don't attempt to select them. Hosts or admins can view past dates as disabled and also mark future dates as unavailable when needed. By supporting both behaviors, the system provides a clear, intuitive experience for different user roles and prevents confusion during date selection.

fields.before: The maximum amount of months displayed in the calendar popover is three.
fields.after:
Range fill color.

The range fill shows which days fall between two selected dates. If the range spans more than the three-month calendar view, it ends on the last visible day but continues as users navigate with the calendar chevrons. A dashed stroke outlines the fill to improve visibility on bright screens and for users with vision impairments.

guideline: Calendar popover states.

fields.before: The minimum amount of months displayed in the calendar popover is one.
fields.after:
Calendar popover states.

The calendar popover supports a disabled state but not a read-only state. Dates or months may be temporarily disabled based on context (for example, if a user must complete a task before selecting a date). In these cases, help text can explain why certain dates are unavailable. If a date picker is truly read-only, users shouldn't be able to open the calendar popover at all, since they can't interact with it.

fields.before: The calendar popover may display an error as error text when a user attempts to provide an input that violates the defined constraints of the date selection. For example, when the user selects dates that fall outside allowable limits, or conflict with contextual restrictions.
fields.after:
Optional time fields.

The calendar popover can also include time-specific fields, allowing users to specify start and end times.

before.description: Whether to show a time zone indicator in the calendar.

after.description: How many months are shown side by side: one, two or three.

fields.before: Controls whether the calendar allows selecting a single date or a date range.
fields.after: Controls whether the calendar allows selecting a single date or a date range. A range adds the range-fill band behind the days between the two selected dates.

after.name: container
after.description: Root of the calendar: holds the header, the weekday labels and the day grid, and owns the 24 gap between the header and the grid and between months. It draws no surface of its own; the popover that holds a calendar is part of the component that opens it (date-picker nests a popover part).

after.name: current-day-indicator
after.description: Marker that sets today's cell apart. Drawn inside the day when its isToday is true.

after.name: day
after.description: One date cell, repeated for every day of every visible month (the days slot). Styled for selected, hover, error, disabled and unavailable.

after.name: focus-indicator
after.description: Outline drawn around the focused day.

after.name: help-text
after.description: Component part: the help-text component, shown with an error message below the calendar when isError is true.

after.name: next-button
after.description: Quiet action-button (component action-button with isQuiet true) that moves to the next month. Drawn on the last visible month.

after.name: previous-button
after.description: Quiet action-button (component action-button with isQuiet true) that moves to the previous month. Drawn on the first visible month.

after.name: range-fill
after.description: Highlight band behind the days between the two ends of a selected range (Figma Highlight fill, selection background). Visible only when selectionMode is range.

after.name: title
after.description: Month and year text of a month (Figma Month + Year, RSP CalendarHeading). Repeated once per visible month.

after.name: unavailable-indicator
after.description: Line struck through the day number of an unavailable day (Figma strikethrough). Drawn inside the day when its isUnavailable is true.

after.name: weekday-label
after.description: Single-letter weekday heading above a month's day grid. Seven per month.

after.name: default
after.description: The day cells. Each entry of the days option is drawn as one copy of the day part, for every visible month.

entries.name: purpose: Calendars display days, weeks, and months, allow

fields.before: Calendars display days, weeks, and months, allowing users to select dates or ranges.
fields.after: Calendars display days, weeks, and months, allowing users to select dates or ranges. One to three months are shown side by side (option visibleMonths). Also called RangeCalendar when selectionMode is range.

A9 (2026-11-21), owner decisions C2, C3, C4, C8, C10 to C15. calendar is the only anatomy; single-, double- and triple-calendar are frozen legacy holders and visibleMonths 1|2|3 replaces them. It draws no popover (date-picker nests the popover). Months are a repeat of title, weekday-label and days, not a part. Nested components (action-button, help-text) are described, not declared: the anatomy component field is not built. range-fill is described as visible for selectionMode range because presentIn takes states, not options. Figma has no Calendar page (Date picker page only); RSP S2 Calendar.

fields.before: Calendars display days, weeks, and months, allowing users to select dates or ranges.
fields.after: Calendars display days, weeks, and months, allowing users to select dates or ranges. One to three months are shown side by side (option visibleMonths). Also called RangeCalendar when selectionMode is range.

after.name: day-fill
after.description: Circle behind the day number: the selected, hover, keyboard-focus and error fill of a day (Figma .Day Calendar Day frame). Drawn over the range-fill band, under the label.

fields.before: Highlight band behind the days between the two ends of a selected range (Figma Highlight fill, selection background). Visible only when selectionMode is range.
fields.after: Highlight band behind a day inside a selected range (Figma .Range fill Highlight fill, selection background). It fills the whole day cell (40 wide) under the day circle, so the bands of consecutive days join into one band. Every selected day draws it, the two ends too: under an end circle (32) it shows as a 4px stub on each side, and its corners are square (the engine has no per-corner radius below the root or per-child alignment, so it is not rounded or flush at the circle edge). A one-day range draws no band. Drawn only when selectionMode is range and the day is selected.

source.title: feat(design-data): calendar range band engine features (stack align, corner radii, row place)

fields.before: Highlight band behind a day inside a selected range (Figma .Range fill Highlight fill, selection background). It fills the whole day cell (40 wide) under the day circle, so the bands of consecutive days join into one band. Every selected day draws it, the two ends too: under an end circle (32) it shows as a 4px stub on each side, and its corners are square (the engine has no per-corner radius below the root or per-child alignment, so it is not rounded or flush at the circle edge). A one-day range draws no band. Drawn only when selectionMode is range and the day is selected.
fields.after: Highlight band behind a day inside a selected range (Figma .Range fill Highlight fill, selection background). It fills the whole day cell (40 wide) under the day circle of a day inside the range, so the bands of consecutive days join into one band. The two ends draw half a cell, from the circle's center to the cell edge, so the band is flush with the circle. The band has pill ends at the ends of a week row. A one-day range draws no band, and neither does an end at a week row edge. Drawn only when selectionMode is range and the day is selected.
